name: The Giant Cypress of the Valley of the Butterflies

location.address: Agios Arsenios - Petaloudes (Valley of the Butterflies), Paros, about 7 km from Parikia

official_register.name: Greek Tree Registry, Friends of Hellenic National Parks (entry 200)

access: Paid entry to the Butterflies Nature Reserve (small admission fee; registry: June to September, 10:00 to 18:00). Registry also says the cypress is visible from the road. Private reserve, so closed outside season.
transport: About 7 km from Parikia (Paros main port) by road; bus or car, real timing to confirm.
story:
The Greek Tree Registry counts this cypress among the largest in Greece, 35 metres tall on a trunk 4.45 metres round.

It grows in the Valley of the Butterflies at Petaloudes, about 7 kilometres from Parikia, inside a private nature reserve on farmland that also lies within a Natura 2000 site. The reserve is home to the jersey tiger, which is a moth, and the valley holds cypresses, ivy-covered planes and wild olives. The valley lies close to the monastery of Agios Arsenios.

Twenty-two metres away stands the cypress's companion, a stone pine 3.3 metres round and 22 metres tall, which the registry also counts among the largest of its kind in Greece. Ivy climbs its trunk, and butterflies live on the ivy leaves. The two trees share one spot, so stand between them and you have both.

The reserve charges a small fee and, according to the registry, opens from June to September, 10:00 to 18:00. Outside those months the gate is shut, but the cypress can still be seen from the road. The pine cannot, so for both trees come in season.

No source gives an age for either tree. If you know more, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, 35 metres, and you can see it from the road. It stands at Petaloudes, 22 metres from a big stone pine with ivy climbing its trunk.
